title: Quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphisms of algebraic stacks
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use algebraic stacks and smooth surjective scheme atlases as in [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], with categories fibred in groupoids, their morphisms and $2$-fibre products as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. A category fibred in groupoids $\mathcal Z$ over $\mathit{Sch}/S$ (for instance an algebraic stack, a $2$-fibre product of algebraic stacks over an algebraic stack or algebraic space, or an algebraic space regarded as a discrete fibred groupoid) is quasi-compact if it admits a smooth surjective atlas $U\to\mathcal Z$ with $U$ a quasi-compact scheme [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. A morphism $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of algebraic stacks, where $\mathcal Y$ may also be an algebraic space, is quasi-compact if for every quasi-compact algebraic stack $\mathcal Z$ and morphism $\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Y$, the $2$-fibre product $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Z$ is quasi-compact. Algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] are regarded as discrete fibred groupoids. A sheaf $A$ on $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$, for instance an algebraic space, is quasi-compact if it admits a representable surjective etale map $h_U\to A$ in the sense of [def-trf-algebraic-space] with $U$ a quasi-compact scheme. A morphism $g:A\to B$ of algebraic spaces is quasi-compact if for every quasi-compact algebraic space $C\to B$, the sheaf fibre product $A\times_B C$ is quasi-compact; it is quasi-separated if its relative diagonal $A\to A\times_B A$ is quasi-compact. The relative diagonal $\Delta_f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ sends an object $x$ to $(x,x,\mathrm{id}_{f(x)})$. The morphism $f$ is quasi-separated if its diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces and quasi-compact and quasi-separated: for every scheme $T\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ is equivalent over $T$ to an algebraic space, and its projection to $T$ has both properties just defined. Representability of the diagonal is part of this predicate, not an assertion about arbitrary morphisms. These predicates impose no finite-type or Deligne--Mumford hypothesis, and make no choice of an atlas.
